top_choice_rationale: P001 awards the optical lattice clock to Katori and Ye, a two-name allocation with a clean credit story. The magic-wavelength lattice is a distinct, mature mechanism (light-shift cancellation, Lamb-Dicke confinement, parallel interrogation of many atoms) that took neutral-atom clocks to the 1e-18 level and is now routinely used in comparisons and new-physics searches. With a citation naming the magic-wavelength scheme and its realisation, it is separable from the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-control prizes. It is a better-defined and more complete case than any alternative, so it ranks above no award.
recusal_note: none apparent for P001; as director of WACQT working on superconducting circuits and circuit QED, I have a field-proximity link to B056, which is not in this slate.
